The term "Eskimo" historically referred to the indigenous peoples of the Arctic and subarctic regions of North America and Siberia. Its etymology is complex; commonly thought to derive from an Algonquian term meaning "eaters of raw meat," later linguistic research suggested it might relate to "one who nets snowshoes." Regardless, many indigenous groups consider the term derogatory, viewing it as a colonial label.
